'''Redshift''', often denoted by $z$, describes the shift in wavelength of light emitted by [[celestial object]]s when observed from elsewhere because of [[cosmic expansion]].<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>

By definition,

{{#content:Q2607}}

== Non-relativistic description  ==

The non-relativistic standard [[Doppler effect]] description is valid for galaxies adequately close to each other to ignore spacetime geometry ($z \ll 1$):

$$
z =\frac{v_r}{c}
$$

where $v_r$ is the relative speed of separation (negative in case of approach) between the observer and the light source.

<ref>{{#cite:Q2580}}</ref>
